title: The Brahmin's Wife and the Mongoose
text:
A brahmin and his wife had a baby son. On the same day a mongoose in the house had a young one, and the wife, who loved small creatures, raised the little mongoose alongside her child, feeding it milk and caring for it like a second son. Yet in her heart she never fully trusted it. It was a wild animal, she thought, and might one day turn on the baby.

One morning she needed to fetch water. She left the baby sleeping, told her husband to keep watch, and went out. But the brahmin soon went off to beg for alms and left the house empty.

While they were gone, a black snake slid out of a hole toward the cradle. The mongoose saw it, attacked, and after a fierce fight tore it to pieces. Proud of what it had done, it ran out to meet the mother, its mouth and paws smeared with blood.

When she saw the blood, she was sure it had killed her son. Without stopping to think, she threw her heavy water pot down on the mongoose and killed it. Then she ran inside, found her baby sleeping safely and the torn body of the snake beside the cradle, and broke down in grief over the loyal animal she had destroyed.
lesson: Fear and haste make us strike before we look. When something alarms you, take a moment to check what really happened before you act.
people: A brahmin's wife, her baby, a mongoose, a snake
caveat: The Panchatantra's date is uncertain, and versions differ on whether the brahmin or his wife kills the mongoose.
